- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-responds to sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.0); add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude to forecast.
- Model often overshoots after strong upward moves (e.g., sentiment > 0.8 for 3+ days); cap forecast at 1.2x recent peak or 1.5x prior 5-day average.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead); increase forecast by 0.5–1.0x the recent mean if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model underestimates late-period sentiment-driven surges; add 0.3–0.7x the sentiment volatility to forecast tail.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.4 → +0.6), model fails to anticipate; adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum direction.
